title: Spanish, B.A. (College of the Liberal Arts)
notes: Entrance to major requires a 2.00 GPA and third-semester classification, not modeled directly. New span_catalog.json (SPAN 1/2/3/100/100A/100B/200/200A/215N/253W). SPAN 1->2->3 is a strict linear prereq chain; SPAN 100 (standard track, used here) and SPAN 100A/100B (heritage-speaker/medical-Spanish tracks) run in parallel, each gated on SPAN 3 or placement, not on each other -- per the bulletin's own note that heritage/native speakers take SPAN 100A/200A instead of the standard sequence. SPAN 215 has no unsuffixed catalog entry -- only SPAN 215N (Gen Ed Inter-Domain) and SPAN 215Q (Honors) exist; modeled as an OR-pool. SPAN 100C and SPAN 100H, cited as prereq alternatives for SPAN 215N/253W, could not be confirmed as standalone courses (absent from the department's full listing, appearing only inside other courses' prereq strings) -- not modeled, documented in span_catalog.json. '200-/300-level SPAN courses' (5 occurrences), '400-level SPAN literature', '400-level SPAN linguistics', and 'three 400-level SPAN courses' (3 occurrences) are modeled as generic slots, matching the bulletin's own open-range phrasing. 'LA 283' (the same unconfirmed code hit throughout recent Liberal Arts builds) replaced with a generic slot. Re-verified against the bulletin's own program-requirements PDF (spanish-ba_programrequirementstext.pdf) for a real handbook-depth pass. Confirmed SPAN 215/253W and SPAN 200/100 modeling is correct (SPAN 215N/215Q share the exact bulletin title 'The Science of Spanish...', confirming they ARE the bare 'SPAN 215' the bulletin cites, just under its Gen Ed-tagged course codes -- not a bug). Found that all 4 previously-generic elective pools ('200-/300-level SPAN Course' x3, '400-level SPAN Literature Course', '400-level SPAN Linguistics Course', '400-level SPAN Course' x3) actually correspond to the bulletin's own real, exactly-enumerated closed lists -- wired up with the real course codes instead of unfillable placeholders: the 9cr Supporting 200-/300-level list (SPAN 220/297/299/300/300B/305/314/315N/316/353/355/356/397/399 -- SPAN 210 and SPAN 354 omitted, stale/unconfirmed codes not in span_catalog.json, same convention as RUS 400), the 3cr '400-level Hispanic Linguistics' list (SPAN 411/417/418/497), the 3cr '400-level Hispanic Literature' list (SPAN 439/470/472/474/476/479/488/490/491/497), and the 9cr 'additional 400-level' list (SPAN 410/411/412/413/417/418/420/439/470/472/474/476/479/488/490/491/497/499). The bulletin's own footnote ('courses may not count in multiple areas') is enforced automatically since a course picked for one item is excluded from every other item in the same build pass. No PSU Romance and Classical Languages and Literatures / Spanish program handbook (beyond the bulletin) could be found published anywhere -- bulletin-only major. 2026-09-18 re-investigation of the docs/MAJORS_NEEDING_REVIEW.md 'LA 83 stated 1.5cr but catalog says 1.0cr' finding: re-scraped https://bulletins.psu.edu/undergraduate/colleges/liberal-arts/spanish-ba/ live (bulletin_scraper.py) and confirmed the bulletin's own Semester 1 plan grid genuinely lists 'LA 83' at 1.5cr (Fall subtotal 17.5cr, matching this file's target_credits) -- LA 83 is a variable-credit (1-3cr) Liberal Arts first-year seminar, and 1.5cr is the real, section-specific credit value the Spanish BA bulletin cites for it. This file's stated "credits": 1.5 on the LA 83 item (line 17) is therefore correct and was left unchanged. The catalog's la_catalog.json entry for LA 83 stores a flat 1.0cr (evidently captured from a different/default section of this variable-credit course), and planner_engine.py's _item_credits() helper (used by build_full_plan/recommend_semester for any "type": "course" item with explicit options) unconditionally prefers the catalog's credit value over the plan item's own stated credits whenever the picked code exists in the catalog -- so LA 83 is actually scheduled at 1.0cr, not this file's 1.5cr. Confirmed by running build_full_plan for SPANBA-2026: Semester 1's engine output totals 17.0cr of required items (not the intended 17.5cr) and, because that leaves 1.0 spare credit under the 18cr/semester cap, the engine additionally recommends an unintended filler elective (SPAN 297, 1.0cr) that would not fit if LA 83 correctly counted as 1.5cr. This is a genuine engine-wide behavior, not a SPANBA-specific data error -- notably, planner_engine.py's own gen_ed slot-picking code (the ge_credits override right before the max_credits check in recommend_semester) already does the OPPOSITE for "type": "slot" gen_ed items, explicitly preferring the item's declared credits over the picked course's own credit count for exactly this reason (documented there for GHW half-credit terms). _item_credits() applies the reverse priority for "type": "course" items, which is inconsistent and produces a wrong per-semester total for any plan item whose real, bulletin-cited credit value differs from the shared catalog's stored value for that course (LA 83 here; likely other variable-credit courses elsewhere). Left unfixed here as an engine-level decision out of scope for this SPANBA-only pass -- see docs/MAJORS_NEEDING_REVIEW.md. UPDATE (2026-09-22): the engine-level inconsistency flagged above is now fixed. _item_credits() (Backend/planner_engine.py) was changed to always prefer a plan item's own explicit "credits" value when it's set, falling back to the shared catalog's stored value only when the item doesn't state credits at all -- matching the priority the "slot" gen_ed-picking logic in the same function already used, and matching plan_progress's own credit accounting (which has always trusted item.get("credits") directly and never read the catalog at all). LA 83 now correctly schedules at this file's own 1.5cr, Semester 1 now correctly totals 17.5cr, and the unintended SPAN 297 filler no longer gets pulled into Semester 1. Regression test: Backend/tests.py TestSpanishBAPlan.test_la_83_schedules_at_its_own_stated_1_5_credits. A repo-wide mismatch scan (item credits vs. catalog credits, across every degree_plans/*.json "type": "course" item with an explicit credits value) found this same pattern affecting roughly 270+ other plan files across ~90 other majors, not just SPANBA -- most were simple stale-catalog-placeholder cases (variable-credit independent-study/thesis/practicum courses, same as LA 83) that the fix now handles correctly automatically. A handful of majors (GEOBIO, GEOSCI, MINE, and EEBH-2022) turned out to have been silently relying on the old, wrong catalog-priority to make a 4-year plan artificially "fit" -- each was independently re-verified against its own official PSU suggested-academic-plan PDF and confirmed to have a genuine, real 9th-term credit overflow once its items' real credit values were honored; see Backend/tests.py's _GRAD_YEARS_OVERRIDE entries for those majors for the full citation trail. MINE-2024/2025/2026.json also had a separate, independent plan-file typo (MNG 412 stated at 2cr instead of the bulletin's real 3cr, unlike MINE-2022/2023.json which already had it right) that this same investigation surfaced and fixed directly in those three files.
